entry_point: Part-time Store Associate / Cashier at 16+ (Walmart Bowmanville, No Frills and other local retailers). No experience required for entry roles.
name: Retail clerk → supervisor → assistant manager
notes: Role ladder is verified from Walmart Canada's own careers page (Store Associate; Store Leadership: Assistant Manager, Co-Manager, Store Manager). All timeframes are GENERAL GUIDANCE, not published by Walmart — promotion depends on performance, hours and openings, and management roles are generally full-time adult roles. Do not present timelines as Walmart policy.

steps.description: Learn the shop floor: customer service, cash, stocking, facing shelves, health and safety. Part-time after school/weekends is the normal teen pattern. No experience required for entry roles.
steps.title: 1. Store Associate / Cashier (entry)

steps.description: Trusted with a department or a shift area: train new starters, handle customer issues, own stock and merchandising standards for one area.
steps.title: 2. Senior Associate / Team Lead / Department Associate

steps.description: Manage a team on a shift: rotas, stock control, coaching, handling escalations. Usually full-time; most teens reach this after leaving school or while at college.
steps.title: 3. Department Supervisor / Department Manager

steps.description: Walmart's own careers page describes Assistant Managers as confident communicators who engage and inspire their teams, and Co-Managers as supporting the Store Manager and coaching associates across departments, on the path to Store Manager. Requires sustained full-time experience.
steps.title: 4. Assistant Manager → Co-Manager → Store Manager

summary: The classic first-job ladder: start on the floor as a teen, build reliability and customer skills, then move into supervising a department and eventually managing a store. Realistic for Owen as a long game, not a quick promotion.

entry_point: Grocery Clerk part-time at No Frills Bowmanville (or Walmart grocery). No Frills lists Grocery Clerk part-time roles with no previous experience required.
name: Grocery clerk → department roles (grocery)
notes: Role titles and the no-experience entry point are verified from Loblaw/No Frills careers listings found 2026-11-16. The Grocery Clerk wage $17.95-$18.45/hr and Department Manager range $17.95-$26.45/hr are from specific Loblaw postings, NOT a Bowmanville posting — do not quote them as Owen's local wage. Department Manager postings require previous management experience in retail/food services and evening/weekend/holiday availability; that step is an adult, usually full-time role. Timeframes are general guidance.

steps.description: Stock shelves, face product, help customers, keep the department neat and safe. No Frills says: 'Good news! No previous experience is required. We provide you with training.' Part-time afternoon/evening shifts fit after school.
steps.title: 1. Grocery Clerk — part-time

steps.description: Take ownership of one section (e.g. dairy, frozen, produce): ordering, rotation, waste control, training newer clerks. Often a step up within the same store.
steps.title: 2. Experienced Clerk / Specialist Clerk

steps.description: No Frills lists a Grocery Assistant Department Manager role (full-time, day). Supports the department manager on sales, staffing and standards.
steps.title: 3. Grocery Assistant Department Manager

steps.description: Own a department's day-to-day operations, sales and team. Loblaw postings say preference is given to candidates with prior department-specific experience and previous management experience in retail or food services. Full-time, evenings/weekends/holidays.
steps.title: 4. Grocery Department Manager

summary: Grocery is one of the most realistic teen employers in Bowmanville (No Frills, Walmart). The ladder is real, but department management is a full-time adult role several years away — the teen win is the clerk job itself plus a specialist-clerk step.

entry_point: Bronze Star (ages 10-12) or Bronze Medallion at 13+. Clarington runs all of these courses locally.
name: Aquatics: swim instructor assistant / lifeguard-in-training → lifeguard
notes: Certification chain, ages and prerequisites verified by opening Clarington's Lifeguarding and Leadership page 2026-11-16 and cross-checked against YMCA GTA's lifeguard page. Course lengths: YMCA GTA lists Bronze Star 10 hrs, Bronze Medallion 15 hrs, Bronze Cross 20 hrs, National Lifeguard 40 hrs; Clarington runs Medallion/Cross over 11 weeks with the exam in week 11. National Lifeguard must be recertified every 2 years (YMCA GTA / Lifesaving Society).

steps.description: Optional head start for ages 10-12: swimming skills, fitness and rescues, in preparation for Bronze Medallion. Clarington also offers a Junior Lifeguard Club.
steps.timeframe: One term (general guidance; course length not stated on Clarington page)
steps.title: 1. Bronze Star (optional, ages 10-12)

steps.description: First lifesaving award. Prerequisite: age 13+ or completed Bronze Star. Includes Emergency (now Basic) First Aid. Prerequisite for all advanced lifesaving programs.
steps.timeframe: 11 weeks in Clarington (exam week 11); ~15 hrs per YMCA GTA
steps.title: 2. Bronze Medallion + Emergency/Basic First Aid

steps.description: Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C/AED — required before National Lifeguard. (Clarington page lists it as a separate step; note the WSIB rename: Standard First Aid is now Intermediate First Aid.)
steps.timeframe: ~16 hours (Clarington describes Standard First Aid as a 16-hour program)
steps.title: 3. Intermediate (Standard) First Aid + CPR-C/AED

steps.description: Advanced lifesaving; begins the transition from lifesaving to lifeguarding and prepares candidates as assistant lifeguards. Prerequisite: Bronze Medallion + Emergency First Aid. This is the prerequisite for Clarington Assistant Lifeguard jobs and all advanced instructor programs.
steps.timeframe: 11 weeks in Clarington (exam week 11); ~20 hrs per YMCA GTA
steps.title: 4. Bronze Cross — assistant lifeguard level

steps.description: Paid teen job: assist lifeguards/instructors at Clarington pools. Clarington lists minimum age 15 and current Bronze Cross (or National Lifeguard) as the minimum qualification.
steps.timeframe: Can apply at 15 once Bronze Cross is held
steps.title: 5. Assistant Lifeguard / Assistant Instructor (first paid aquatics job)

steps.description: The industry-accepted standard for lifeguards in Canada and the only lifeguard certificate recognised by Ontario for public pools (YMCA GTA). Prerequisites: age 15, Bronze Cross, Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C. Also the route to Swim Instructor (15+, Bronze Cross) and Lifesaving Society Instructor (15+, Bronze Cross).
steps.timeframe: ~40 hours per YMCA GTA; recertify every 2 years
steps.title: 6. National Lifeguard (and/or Swim Instructor) — qualified lifeguard

summary: The clearest credential ladder available to a Bowmanville teen: every step is a published course, run locally by Clarington, with a paid job (Assistant Lifeguard at 15) in the middle and full lifeguard at 15-16. Costs exist per course and were not listed on the page — check BeActive; a 25% discount applies if a Clarington course was taken in the past 3 years.

entry_point: Grade 11 or 12 co-op in a trade, via the school co-op/guidance teacher. OYAP participants must be at least 15 and have 14+ secondary credits (per YRDSB; some boards say 16+ — confirm with the school).
name: Trades via OYAP apprenticeship (electrician, carpenter, plumber)
notes: OYAP structure verified via YRDSB and PVNCCDSB OYAP pages in search results 2026-11-16. No Durham District School Board / Kawartha Pine Ridge OYAP page was opened — Owen must confirm the local process with his own school's co-op teacher/guidance, since the school arranges the placement. Apprenticeship length 2-5 years (80% on-the-job / 20% in-class) comes from the TCDSB OYAP guide. Trade examples (electrician, carpenter, plumber) are listed on the YRDSB page.

steps.description: Talk to the school co-op teacher/guidance in Grade 10 course selection. Take related tech courses (construction, electrical, etc.) and keep grades/attendance strong — OYAP pages list commitment, good work habits and regular attendance as requirements.
steps.title: 1. Explore in school, pick a trade direction

steps.description: In Grade 11 or 12, take a 2-credit (half-day) or 4-credit (full-day) co-op placement in an apprenticeable trade, linked to a related high-school credit. The co-op learning plan includes competencies from the trade's Apprenticeship Training Standards log book. Sign an OYAP Participant Form.
steps.title: 2. OYAP Participant — co-op placement in a trade

steps.description: If the placement employer agrees, sign a Registered Training Agreement with Skilled Trades Ontario and start accumulating registered apprenticeship hours/competencies while still in high school.
steps.title: 3. Register as an apprentice (OYAP Registered Student)

steps.description: In the final semester of high school, eligible students can complete all/part of Level 1 apprenticeship schooling at a college or training centre while earning high-school credits, with a registered employer sponsor.
steps.title: 4. Accelerated (Level 1) OYAP — optional fast track

steps.description: After graduation, continue as a paid apprentice: ~80% paid on-the-job training with a journeyperson sponsor, ~20% in-class blocks, over 2-5 years depending on trade, through to journeyperson certification (Certificate of Qualification where applicable).
steps.title: 5. Full apprenticeship → journeyperson

summary: OYAP lets a high-school student start a real trade while earning diploma credits — the only path here where school itself is the entry point. It needs planning a year ahead (course selection + co-op teacher), not a walk-in application.

entry_point: Volunteer at 13+ (Clarington Youth Centres, library, community programs) or Leader-in-Training / Counsellor-in-Training programs at 14-15; paid camp counsellor at 16.
name: Recreation / camp counsellor → program leader
notes: Ages and qualifications verified: Clarington camp counsellor roles require minimum age 16 (Clarington March Break Inclusion Counsellor posting and Program Instructor 2 posting found in search); Hamilton's recreation jobs page (comparable Ontario municipality) states Camp Counsellor 16+, Standard First Aid with CPR-C, and that the minimum volunteer age is 13. The CIT/LIT step is from a named Ontario camp (Hockey Opportunity Camp) — it is an example of how the step works, not a Clarington program. Later steps (senior counsellor, program leader) are GENERAL GUIDANCE.

steps.description: Build experience supervising children: volunteer at CYC, the library, or a local camp/sport program. Minimum volunteer age 13 in Ontario municipal recreation (Hamilton page). Volunteer hours also count toward the Ontario 40-hour community-service requirement.
steps.title: 1. Volunteer / Leader-in-Training (LIT)

steps.description: Application-based leadership training (example: Hockey Opportunity Camp CIT, ages 15-16 just after Grade 10; 2-4 week sessions in leadership, mentoring, counselling and activity instruction, sometimes with Bronze Cross). Clarington itself runs Leadership Camp / Counsellor-in-Training camps — confirm current offerings on the Clarington recreation pages.
steps.title: 2. Counsellor-in-Training (CIT)

steps.description: Plan and deliver activities for a group of children (typically 8-12 kids, ages 4-12). Clarington and other Ontario municipalities require age 16 and Standard First Aid with CPR-C. Clarington hires March Break and summer camp counsellors; part-time roles average 24 hrs/week or less.
steps.title: 3. Camp Counsellor (paid, 16+)

steps.description: Lead a cabin/section, mentor junior counsellors, own an activity area. Usually needs 1-2 summers as a counsellor plus Standard First Aid/CPR-C (Clarington Program Instructor 2 posting: at least 16, 1-2 years' experience working with children in recreation, leadership qualities).
steps.title: 4. Senior Counsellor / Program Instructor

steps.description: Own a camp or program area: staff supervision, scheduling, parent contact, safety. Typically an adult/college-age role; builds directly on senior counsellor experience and can lead toward recreation management or teaching/child-care careers.
steps.title: 5. Camp Supervisor / Program Leader

summary: The summer-jobs ladder: volunteer young, train at 15-16, get paid at 16, lead by 17-18. Very realistic for Owen, but it is seasonal — the counsellor job is a summer job, so it pairs with a school-year retail/grocery job rather than replacing it.

entry_point: Part-time customer-service / front-end associate at 16+ (retail, recreation customer service, call centre — only where the employer hires under-18s).
name: Customer service → sales / team lead
notes: This path is the least formally documented of the six: the role ladder (associate → senior → supervisor) is consistent with Walmart Canada's store careers page, but NO employer was found publishing a customer-service-specific progression with timelines. All steps after entry are GENERAL GUIDANCE and the whole path is marked accordingly. Treat it as a plausible direction, not a sourced progression.

steps.description: Greet customers, answer questions, handle returns and complaints calmly, learn the till/POS and the store's products. The transferable skill is dealing with people under pressure.
steps.title: 1. Customer Service Associate (entry)

steps.description: Handle escalations, train new associates on service standards, own a service desk or department's customer experience. Product knowledge becomes the edge — this is where sales skills (recommending, upselling honestly) start to matter.
steps.title: 2. Senior Associate / Customer Service Lead

steps.description: Run a shift's front end or service team, manage rotas and cash handling, coach the team on service and sales targets.
steps.title: 3. Customer Service Supervisor / Front-End Supervisor

steps.description: Move into a sales-focused role (department sales, electronics, telecom kiosks) or a team-lead role with sales targets; from there, department/assistant management. Sales roles often add commission or bonuses — confirm per employer, not assumed here.
steps.title: 4. Sales Associate / Team Lead → management

summary: Customer service is the skill every other path uses; as a standalone ladder it is slower and less documented than retail or aquatics. Best read as: take a service job for the skills, and let it feed into retail supervision or sales later.
